Variants.Content: Fresh water, one of the most stringent restrictions on a voyage, was usually stored in wooden barrels and rationed on a daily basis. Water can become stale, grow filth, or be lost through cracks in barrels; ships must therefore calculate replenishment ports and rainy seasons, and a lack of water often destroys discipline faster than a lack of food.
